prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Reform UK’s 2024 “Contract with You” sets out a programme to “reset” the UK, arguing Labour and Conservatives have failed. It prioritises tighter borders, tax cuts, public service reform, cheaper energy, and cultural and constitutional changes, funded by large savings and deregulation.

Core pledges
- Freeze non‑essential immigration; stop small boats and detain/deport illegal arrivals.
- End NHS waiting lists while keeping care free at point of use.
- Make work pay: raise the income tax threshold to £20,000.
- Cut energy bills by scrapping Net Zero and unlocking domestic oil and gas.
- Restore law and order.

Key policies
- Immigration: Exit the ECHR if needed; create a Department of Immigration; no asylum from safe countries; offshore processing; no legal aid for non‑citizens; immediate deportation of foreign criminals; bar student dependents; five‑year residency/work to access benefits; employer immigration NI at 20% (exempt essential health/care and micro firms).
- Government waste: Stop paying interest on QE reserves; require every department to cut 5% waste; halve foreign aid; cull retained EU laws; improve HMRC tax collection.
- Personal economy: Lift income tax start point to £20k (higher rate from £70k); cut fuel duty by 20p, scrap VAT and green levies on energy; big stamp duty cuts; restore VAT‑free shopping; exempt estates under £2m from IHT (20% above, with charity option).
- Business: Raise CT threshold to £100k profit; cut CT rate to 20%, then 15% (Yr 3); abolish IR35; lift VAT threshold to £150k; later abolish business rates for high‑street SMEs, offset by a 4% online delivery tax; speed planning; slash red tape and ease hiring/firing; simplify tax code.
- NHS: Zero basic rate tax for frontline NHS/social care staff for 3 years; end training caps; write off fees via service; use independent/overseas capacity; 20% tax relief on private care/insurance; guarantee waits via vouchers; operational efficiencies; inquiry into excess deaths/vaccine harms.
- Energy/Net Zero: Scrap Net Zero and renewable subsidies; fast‑track North Sea and shale pilots; pursue SMRs, gas, tidal, lithium.
- Policing/Justice: Recruit 40,000 officers; zero‑tolerance; expand stop and search; scrap DEI roles; increase justice budget; redefine hate crime; build 10,000 prison places; tougher repeat‑offender sentences; anti‑grooming measures; youth training camps.
- Education: “Patriotic” curriculum; ban gender transitioning/pronoun changes in schools; 20% tax relief on independent school fees; scrap interest on student loans and extend repayment; strengthen free speech; expand PRUs; offer 2‑year degrees.
- Benefits: Two‑strike rule for job offers; face‑to‑face assessments; incentives and apprenticeships to get up to 2m back to work.
- Brexit: Scrap remaining EU laws; abandon the Windsor Framework; prepare to renegotiate the TCA.
- Defence: Raise spending to 2.5% of GDP by Yr 3 and 3% within 6 years; pay rises; Armed Forces Justice Bill; a dedicated Veterans department; recruit 30,000 for the Army; procurement reform.
- Housing: Fast‑track brownfield; prioritize locals for social housing; restore mortgage interest deductibility for landlords; scrap Renters’ Reform Bill; leasehold protections.
- Families: Transferable marriage allowance (25%); front‑load child benefit (ages 1‑4); mandate single‑sex spaces; tighter controls on child social media/smartphones.
- Transport/Utilities: Scrap HS2; ban ULEZ/LTNs and most 20mph zones; accelerate regional road/rail; new 50/50 public–UK pension fund utility ownership; cap standing charges.
- Agriculture/Fisheries: Increase farm budget to £3bn; scrap climate‑linked subsidies; protect country sports; restrict foreign fishing, ban supertrawlers; rebuild UK processing.
- Pensions/Social care: Royal Commission; curb offshore tax avoidance by care providers; review pensions; fix Mineworkers scheme.
- Constitutional/Culture: Leave ECHR; reform Lords and civil service; restrict postal voting; PR referendum; British Bill of Rights; reject WHO treaty/WEF/CBDC; replace Equalities Act and DEI rules; Free Speech Bill; scrap BBC licence fee; anti‑corruption unit; make St George’s/St David’s Day holidays.

Funding (claimed): £150bn annual savings + £10bn extra tax from growth = £160bn vs £141bn annual costs; plus one‑off £25bn from scrapping HS2.
